Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1443
Claimant:
Sarah Porter
Adjuster:
Jerry Hanson
4-1-25
Claim opened after a report of a minor collision in a parking lot. The claimant, who is not represented by counsel,
reported neck pain and was advised to seek medical attention.
4-14-25
Spoke with the claimant by phone. Their account of the impact was consistent with the initial report, and they
described the vehicle as having been stopped when the other car reversed into it.
6-13-25
The police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The responding officer recorded
the location and the position of both cars.
6-30-25
Reviewed the photographs submitted by the claimant. They show damage to the rear bumper and tail light area,
which is mostly in line with the impact described. No independent witnesses have come forward.
7-20-25
Confirmed with the insured that the driver involved is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time
of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.
7-24-25
Obtained the vehicle's prior claim and repair history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded, and the repair
esitmate has been scheduled for review.
7-26-25
The claimant's medical records show initial treatment with a physician, followed by a usual course of physiotherapy.
The reported injury fits the kind and force of the collision.
7-30-25
Checked the claimant's history for any prior neck or upper back complaints. None is known, and the claimant has told
the same account in every conversation so far.
8-3-25
Follow-up call with the claimant. Symptoms have eased steadily, and the treatment plan is winding down as they
recover.
10-3-25
Reviewed the file as a whole. The claim is progressing as expected, with the medical treatment tapering as recovery
continues, and the repair estimate is pending final sign-off.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
